questions.title: My first review case
questions.summary: Return customer_id, name and revenue for every customer.
questions.task: Explain why a LEFT JOIN can lose unmatched customers when the right table is filtered in WHERE.
requirements: Use exact output column names and customer_id ordering.
questions.solution: A right-table predicate in WHERE can discard the null-extended unmatched rows. Put the match constraint in ON when those left rows must be preserved.
questions.explanation: Putting paid status inside ON preserves the null-extended customer row. COALESCE turns a missing sum into zero. The output grain is one customer, not one order.
hints: State the output grain, failure boundary, or state transition before choosing a tool.
followUps: What changes when the input is empty, duplicated, late, or retried?
Which observation would validate your answer in a real environment?
rubric: Use exact output column names and customer_id ordering.

visual.detail: Ada matches two paid orders; Cleo and Dan keep one NULL-extended row each. A WHERE filter on o.status would remove them.
